kw: why did you do a phd
intents.answer: I found out during my master's that I really liked research 🔬 So instead of going straight to industry, I stayed for the PhD.
Fun fact: I play piano 🎹

My research sits where cybersecurity meets machine learning 🔐🤖 Mainly: black-box adversarial ML attacks in live networks, social media spam detection, AI-assisted driver awareness at busy intersections, and ML-based activity classification.
intents.more: The adversarial ML work is a big thread for me. Instead of attacking classifiers on offline datasets, we look at how black-box attacks actually behave in live network environments. You can read it [here](https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2026/146389/146389.pdf) 📄

intents.answer: Right now I'm building a tool that creates lab environments for students just from a prompt 🛠️

My favorite is the [cost-effective tool for senior activity classification and visualization](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-13056-3_20) 💙 I already had the hardware lying around and was just playing with it, and once we got the idea, we decided to write the paper.

Here are my recent ones 📄
• [AI-Assisted Driver Situational Awareness at High Density Intersections](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11527458) (IEEE, 2026)
• [Black-Box Adversarial ML Attacks in Live Networks](https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2026/146389/146389.pdf) (ICISSP 2026)
• [Senior Activity Classification and Visualization](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-13056-3_20) (AIR-RES 2025)
• Social media spam detection ([book chapter](#publications), [IEEE CSCE 2023](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10487569))
intents.more: The senior activity one is my favorite, and the full list with authors is in the [Publications](#publications) section 👇

intents.answer: That's my ICISSP 2026 paper 🛡️ We looked at how black-box adversarial ML attacks behave in live network environments, not just on offline datasets. You can read it [here](https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2026/146389/146389.pdf).
intents.more: Real networks are messy, so an attack that works great on a clean dataset doesn't always hold up live. That gap is what makes it interesting to me 🤓

intents.answer: Two things there! 🚗 I co-authored an IEEE paper on [AI-assisted driver situational awareness at high-density intersections](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11527458), and I built a real-time object detection pipeline that logs local vehicle traffic. [Here's the live dashboard](traffic.html) 📊

My master's thesis was about building a versatile tool for social media spam detection 📬 It turned into an IEEE CSCE 2023 paper and a 2025 book chapter with De Gruyter Brill. [Read the thesis](https://etd.ohiolink.edu/acprod/odb_etd/ws/send_file/send?accession=toledo1683279391214158&disposition=inline).

That's my AIR-RES 2025 paper, and honestly my favorite one 💙 It's a cost-effective tool that classifies and visualizes senior activity. I had the hardware lying around, started playing with it, and the idea came from there. [It's on Springer](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-13056-3_20).

A couple of personal ones 🛠️
• [Browser Fingerprinting & OSINT Inspector](inspector.html): shows how much your browser leaks about you without asking.
• [Real-Time Traffic Analytics Pipeline](traffic.html): object detection that keeps logging local vehicle traffic.
intents.more: I also built and run a Proxmox-based virtual lab that supports 50+ students across two courses 🖥️ And right now I'm building a tool that creates lab environments for students just from a prompt.

intents.answer: The Browser Fingerprinting & OSINT Inspector uses plain client-side Web APIs to show what your browser gives away: hardware, network, environment details 🕵️ [Try it on yourself](inspector.html), it's a little scary.

I'm strongest on the systems side 🐧 setting up and managing Proxmox servers, deploying containerized services, Linux command-line work, and automating everything I can. I built a production-grade Proxmox lab that supports 50+ students across two courses.
intents.more: On the ML side I work on adversarial attacks, spam detection, and classification models, so I bounce between infrastructure and research a lot 🔄
